column2: On the authority of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace), the truthful one, the one believed, narrated to us:

“The creation of each one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days as a drop, then he becomes a clinging clot for a like period, then a lump of flesh for a like period. Then the angel is sent to him, breathes the soul into him, and is commanded with four words: he writes down his provision, his lifespan,

his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy. By Allah, besides whom there is no god, one of you will do the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is only a forearm's length between him and it, then what is written overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters it.

And one of you will do the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is only a forearm's length between him and it, then what is written overtakes him, and he does the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters it.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
Al-ṣādiq (“the truthful one”): the one who informs of the truth.
Al-maṣdūq (“the one believed”): the one to whom Allah has been true in His promise.
Inna aḥadakum (“the creation of each one of you”): with kasrah on the hamzah of inna, as a quotation of the wording of the Prophet ﷺ; fatḥah (anna) is also permissible.
Yujmaʿu khalquhu (“his creation is gathered”): its parts are joined together after being dispersed.
What is meant by his creation is its material, which is the fluid from which he is created.
“In his mother's womb (baṭn)”: in her uterus.
Nuṭfah (“a drop”): semen. The basic meaning of nuṭfah is a small amount of fluid.
ʿAlaqah (“a clinging clot”): a piece of blood.
“For a like period”: of time, namely forty [days].
Muḍghah (“a lump of flesh”): a piece of flesh.
“For a like period”: of time, namely forty [days].
“Then the angel is sent to him”: the one entrusted with the womb.

Bi-katbi (“to write down”): it has been vocalised in two ways. The first is with the single-dotted bāʾ carrying kasrah, the kāf fatḥah, the double-dotted tāʾ sukūn, and then the bāʾ (bi-katbi), as an appositive.

The other is with [the yāʾ] carrying fatḥah, in the form of the present tense (yaktubu, “he writes”); this is the stronger reading, because in one narration it reads, “He is given leave with four words, so he writes”, and likewise in the narration of Abū Dāwūd and others.
Rizqahu (“his provision”): its measure, little or much, and its nature, unlawful or lawful.
Wa-ajalahu (“and his lifespan”): long or short; it is the duration of life.
Wa-ʿamalahu (“and his deeds”): righteous or corrupt.

“And whether wretched or happy”: in the nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, that is, “he is wretched or happy”. What is meant is that Allah the Exalted discloses to the angel the provision, lifespan, deeds, wretchedness and happiness mentioned, and commands him to write them down and carry them out.
“The deeds of the people of Paradise”: acts of obedience.
Ḥattā mā yakūnu (“until there is only”): ḥattā here makes the verb subjunctive, and mā is negative.
It is also permissible to put yakūnu in the indicative, with ḥattā introducing a new clause.
“Then what is written overtakes him”: what it contains prevails over him.
“The deeds of the people of the Fire”: acts of disobedience.
An indication of knowledge of the beginning and the return, and of what relates to the human body and its state of wretchedness or happiness.
Swearing an oath on a true report to make it firm in the listener's mind.

Drawing attention to the truth of the resurrection after death: the One able to create a person from a despised fluid, move him on to the clinging clot, then to the lump of flesh, and then breathe the soul into him,
is able to breathe the soul into him after he has become dust, and to gather his parts after they have been scattered. He was able to create him all at once,

but wisdom required moving him through the stages mentioned out of gentleness to the mother, since she was not accustomed to it and the hardship would have been too great for her; so He prepared him in her womb gradually until he was complete.
Whoever reflects on the origin of his own creation is duty-bound to worship his Lord as He truly deserves, and to obey Him and not disobey Him.
Affirming the decree, and that all events happen by the decision and decree of Allah, their good and their bad.
Encouragement to contentment,
and a rebuke of intense greed, because provision has already been measured out. Earning was prescribed only because it is among the means that wisdom requires in the abode of this world.
No one should be deceived by his outward state, since the outcome is unknown; for this reason supplicating for steadfastness in the religion and a good ending has been prescribed.
Repentance demolishes what came before it.
Whoever dies in some state is judged according to it, good or bad, except that those who commit sins other than disbelief are subject to Allah's will.
Wretchedness and happiness have already been written, they are determined according to the endings of deeds, and everyone is eased towards what he was created for.
